answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Each submission hangs on the island of a task receipt, and the anchor is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, held in escrow until finality, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Reaching the quartz of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
